cards.front: Recall a key point about Verbs & Conjugations
cards.back: Latin verbs are conjugated (change form) to show person (1st, 2nd, 3rd), number (singular, plural), tense (when), voice (active/passive), and mood (indicative/subjunctive).

cards.front: Recall a key point about Verbs & Conjugations
cards.back: There are four conjugations, identified by the characteristic vowel in the present stem: 1st (-a-), 2nd (-e-), 3rd (short -e- or consonant), 4th (-i-).

cards.front: Recall a key point about Verbs & Conjugations
cards.back: Every Latin verb has four principal parts that must be memorised: e.g. laudo, laudare, laudavi, laudatus (I praise, to praise, I praised, praised).

cards.front: Recall a key point about Verbs & Conjugations
Recall a key point about Verbs & Conjugations
cards.back: Imperfect tense is formed by adding -ba- plus personal endings to the present stem: e.g. laudabam (I was praising).

cards.front: Recall a key point about Verbs & Conjugations
cards.back: Perfect tense uses the third principal part stem with -v- or -u- endings: e.g. laudavi (I praised), laudavisti (you praised).

cards.front: Recall a key point about Verbs & Conjugations
cards.back: The passive voice reverses the action: the subject receives the verb’s action (e.g. laudor — I am praised; laudatus sum — I was praised).

cards.front: Recall a key point about Verbs & Conjugations
Recall a key point about Verbs & Conjugations
cards.back: Irregular verbs must be learned individually: sum (to be), possum (to be able), eo (to go), volo (to want), nolo (not to want), malo (to prefer).

cards.front: Recall a key point about Verbs & Conjugations
cards.back: The infinitive (e.g. laudare — to praise) is the second principal part and is used to identify the conjugation.

cards.front: What should you know about gcse latin exam tips — verbs & conjugations?
cards.back: 1. For Verbs & Conjugations, use a range of vocabulary and complex grammatical structures to access higher marks 2. Check verb tenses, agreements and word order carefully in your written work 3. In translation tasks, translate meaning rather than word-for-word 4. When writing about Verbs & Conjugations, include opinions and justifications, not just descriptions 5. For listening and reading, focus on key words and cognates to extract meaning
Explain how Latin verbs are conjugated, comparing the formation of the present, imperfect, and perfect tenses in the active voice. Use the verb laudo as your example. (6 marks)

AO1 (Knowledge & Understanding): Demonstrate knowledge and understanding of verbs & conjugations, including Latin language forms, literary techniques, and Roman cultural context.
